title: Leyre Project Grant — Carboplatin Overdosing vs eGFRcr-cys / Cockcroft-Gault Discordance
text:
A focused, grant-ready cut of the OncoGFR 1200 analysis (Leyre project). The cohort and the full exploratory analysis live on the Leyre project site; patient-level data is read by absolute path from that project and is never copied into this repository.
The discordance index on the x-axis here is the same quantity as egfr_difference on the Sherley carboplatin page of this site — (eGFRcr-cys − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault × 100, both in absolute mL/min — measured in a different cohort, and the −10 % marker is the same cutoff. Four figures:

Figure 1 — the probability that carboplatin (Calvert AUC 5, ±20 % band) is overdosed relative to measured GFR, as a smooth function of the eGFR discordance index. One line only (red), one panel per eGFR dosing equation.
Figure 2 — how the 1,200 participants are distributed across that same discordance index.
Figure 3 — the two superimposed: overdose curve over the cohort distribution.
Figure 4 — overdose risk at 10 %, 15 % and 20 %, by frailty and cachexia.



\[
\text{eGFR \% difference} \;=\; \frac{\text{eGFR}_{\text{cr-cys}} - \text{CrCl}_{\text{Cockcroft-Gault}}}{\text{CrCl}_{\text{Cockcroft-Gault}}} \times 100
\]
Both terms are on the absolute mL/min scale (actual body surface area, not indexed to 1.73 m²), i.e. CKDEPIcrcys21non_index and CGnon_index. eGFRcr-cys is the CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine–cystatin C equation.
Negative = cystatin-informed eGFR reads below Cockcroft-Gault, i.e. Cockcroft-Gault is flattering the kidney → the patient is at risk of receiving too much drug. Positive = the reverse.



Carboplatin is dosed by the Calvert formula at AUC 5. A patient is overdosed when the dose computed from the estimating equation exceeds the dose that measured GFR (⁵¹Cr-EDTA) would have given by more than 20 %:
\[5\,(\text{eGFR} + 25) \;>\; 6\,(\text{mGFR} + 25)\]
Measured GFR is the gold standard throughout. Each panel title names the equation used to pick the dose; the x-axis discordance index is the same in every panel.

title: Leyre Project Grant — Carboplatin Overdosing vs eGFRcr-cys / Cockcroft-Gault Discordance
text:
The same curve as numbers
The LOESS panels above in citable form: the observed carboplatin (±20 %) overdose rate within bands of the discordance index, for the two creatinine-based equations a clinic would actually dose from. Absolute mL/min scale, measured GFR as reference.


Code
BANDS <- c(-Inf, -30, -20, -10, 0, 10, Inf)
BAND_LABS <- c("< −30 %", "−30 to −20 %", "−20 to −10 %", "−10 to 0 %",
               "0 to +10 %", "> +10 %")

stratum_tbl <- carbo_nonindex %>%
  dplyr::filter(equation %in% c("CG", "CKDEPIcr21"), !is.na(cls),
                !is.na(egfr_pctdiff_cg)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    band = cut(egfr_pctdiff_cg, BANDS, labels = BAND_LABS, right = FALSE),
    eqn  = factor(equation, levels = c("CG", "CKDEPIcr21"),
                  labels = c("Cockcroft-Gault", "CKD-EPI Cr 2021"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(eqn, band) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(N = dplyr::n(),
                   over = sum(cls == "Overdose"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct = sprintf("%.1f%%", over / N * 100)) %>%
  dplyr::select(eqn, band, N, over, pct) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = eqn, values_from = c(over, pct),
                     names_glue = "{eqn}_{.value}") %>%
  # pivot_wider orders columns by VALUE (both n's, then both %'s). Regroup them
  # by EQUATION so the "Dosed by ..." header spanners sit over the right pairs.
  dplyr::select(band, N,
                `Cockcroft-Gault_over`, `Cockcroft-Gault_pct`,
                `CKD-EPI Cr 2021_over`, `CKD-EPI Cr 2021_pct`) %>%
  dplyr::rename(`eGFR % difference` = band)

stratum_tbl %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>%
  flextable::set_header_labels(
    `Cockcroft-Gault_over` = "n overdosed", `Cockcroft-Gault_pct` = "% overdosed",
    `CKD-EPI Cr 2021_over` = "n overdosed", `CKD-EPI Cr 2021_pct` = "% overdosed") %>%
  flextable::add_header_row(
    values = c("", "", "Dosed by Cockcroft-Gault", "Dosed by CKD-EPI Cr 2021"),
    colwidths = c(1, 1, 2, 2)) %>%
  flextable::align(i = 1, part = "header", align = "center") %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header") %>%
  flextable::autofit()

title: Sherley Project — Grant Figures
text:
Grant-figure versions of the Carboplatin Cohort analyses, re-expressed on the eGFR difference scale.
\[
\text{eGFR difference (\%)} \;=\; \frac{\text{eGFR}_{\text{CR-CYS}} - \text{CrCl}_{\text{CG}}}{\text{CrCl}_{\text{CG}}} \times 100
\]
Both terms in the numerator are in mL/min: the CKD-EPI creatinine–cystatin C eGFR is the version adjusted for actual body surface area (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex, mL/min — not the 1.73 m²-indexed ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys), matching the units of Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. The result is expressed as a percentage: 0 % means the two estimators agree, +20 % means CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 20 % higher than Cockcroft-Gault, −20 % means 20 % lower.






NoteRelationship to the eGFR ratio used on the Carboplatin page



Because egfr_difference = 100 × ((eGFR − CG) / CG) = 100 × (egfr_ratio − 1), this is a pure re-centring and rescaling of the eGFR ratio: the reference point moves from 1 to 0 %. The underlying Fine-Gray fits are therefore the same models as §9 of the Sherley project’s Carboplatin Cohort page — identical p-values. The reported subHRs differ only because this page reports them per 10 % decrease in eGFR difference, whereas §9 reports per 0.1-unit increase in the ratio; the two are reciprocals of each other.

# Output directory for downloadable PowerPoint plots (plots/grant/<name>.pptx).
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/plots/grant", winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
dir.create(pptx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Save the given ggplot as an editable PowerPoint slide via rvg::dml, named by
# the calling chunk's label. Mirrors the helper in the Sherley project's
# sherley_carbo.qmd; the
# post-render script scripts/inject_pptx_links.py then injects a per-plot
# download link beneath each figure in the rendered HTML.
.save_plot_pptx <- function(p, name = NULL) {
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (is.null(name)) {
    name <- tryCatch(knitr::opts_current$get("label"), error = function(e) NULL)
  }
  if (is.null(name)) return(invisible(NULL))
  safe <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", name)
  out  <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(safe, ".pptx"))
  ok <- tryCatch({
    pp <- officer::read_pptx()
    pp <- officer::add_slide(pp, layout = "Title and Content", master = "Office Theme")
    pp <- officer::ph_with(
      pp,
      value = rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
      location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body")
    )
    print(pp, target = out)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  invisible(if (ok) paste0("plots/grant/", safe, ".pptx") else NULL)
}

# Format the exposure-effect subtitle: subHR (or HR) per `scale` units with
# 95% Wald CI and p-value, extracted from the Fine-Gray / Cox PH fit.
.hr_subtitle <- function(beta, V_beta, scale = 1,
                         hr_type = "subHR",
                         unit_label = "per 1-unit increase") {
  se   <- sqrt(V_beta)
  hr   <- exp(beta * scale)
  b1   <- exp((beta - 1.96 * se) * scale)
  b2   <- exp((beta + 1.96 * se) * scale)
  # A negative `scale` (reporting per unit DECREASE) reverses the bound order,
  # so sort rather than assuming b1 <= b2.
  lcl  <- min(b1, b2)
  ucl  <- max(b1, b2)
  pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(beta / se)))
  p_str <- ifelse(pval < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pval))
  sprintf("%s = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f), p = %s   (%s)",
          hr_type, hr, lcl, ucl, p_str, unit_label)
}

# Placeholder for outcomes whose design matrix is singular on this sub-cohort.
.plot_failed <- function(label = "Model could not be fit") {
  p <- ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
             label = paste0(label, "\n(singular design — cohort too small)"),
             size = 3.5) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    theme_void()
  .save_plot_pptx(p)
  p
}

# Analysis data is produced by the Sherley project's data pipeline
# (Sherley/qmd/sherley_data.qmd writes this file). Load the whole cohort, then
# keep only carboplatin patients.

dat <- readRDS(sherley_rds) %>%
  filter(platin_group == "Carboplatin")

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # BSA-adjusted CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (mL/min) vs Cockcroft-Gault CrCl (mL/min).
    # Relative difference expressed as a PERCENT; 0 % = the two estimators agree.
    egfr_difference = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    # Binary exposures for the adjusted CIF sections (§6, §7.3). dose_diff_pct
    # comes from the data pipeline:
    #   100 * (carbo_dose_redcap - carbo_dose_cre_cys) / carbo_dose_cre_cys
    egfr_diff_lt_neg10 = as.integer(egfr_difference < -10),
    dose_pct_ge10      = as.integer(dose_diff_pct >= 10)
  )

title: Sherley Project — Grant Figures
text:
7.1 Distribution
Bins are 10 % wide with an axis tick at every bin edge. The red dashed line marks +10 %, the excess-dose cutoff.


Code
dose_hist <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(dose_diff_pct))

ggplot(dose_hist, aes(x = dose_diff_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 10, boundary = 0,
                 fill = "steelblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", color = "red",
             linewidth = 1.1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Dose Discrepancy (Carboplatin)",
       subtitle = "(administered − eGFR Cr-Cys-predicted dose) / predicted dose × 100;  red line = +10 % excess-dose cutoff",
       x = "Dose discrepancy (%)",
       y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-100, 200, 10)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey25")) -> p
.save_plot_pptx(p)
p

qd <- quantile(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct, c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))
n_dd         <- nrow(dose_hist)
n_excess10   <- sum(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct >= 10)
pct_excess10 <- 100 * n_excess10 / n_dd
n_under10    <- sum(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct <= -10)
n_within10   <- sum(abs(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct) < 10)
n_overlap    <- sum(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct >= 10 &
                      dose_hist$egfr_difference < -10, na.rm = TRUE)
r_dd_egfr    <- cor(dose_hist$dose_diff_pct, dose_hist$egfr_difference,
                    use = "complete.obs")

A total of 34 (28.1%) patients received an excess dose of carboplatin, defined as ≥ 10 % higher than the dose that would have been predicted using the CKD-EPI eGFRCR-CYS equation adjusted for actual BSA. (Denominator: 121 carboplatin patients with a computable predicted dose.)
All 34 of these patients also have an eGFR difference < −10 % (§3), and the two percentages are strongly inversely correlated (r = -0.93): administered doses closely track the Cockcroft-Gault-based dose (§4), so a CKD-EPI Cr-Cys eGFR well below Cockcroft-Gault shows up as an excess dose. The excess-dose group is therefore nearly a subset of the eGFR-difference randomization group, and §7.3 largely echoes §6.

title: Sherley Project — Grant Figures
text:
7.2 Linear subHR Curves — Dose Discrepancy (%)
Same outcomes, adjusters and layout as §5, with the exposure being the dose discrepancy in percent. Reported subHRs are per 10 % increase in dose discrepancy (more drug given than eGFRCR-CYS predicts), so a subHR above 1 means a larger excess dose carries higher risk. Curves are relative to the cohort median (dotted vertical line) and trimmed to the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles.


Code
plot_subhr_dosepct <- function(time_var, status_var, extra_adj = NULL,
                               outcome_label) {
  plot_subhr_linear_diff(time_var, status_var, extra_adj, outcome_label,
                         x_var = "dose_diff_pct", scale = 10,
                         unit_label = "per 10% increase",
                         x_lab = "Dose discrepancy (%)",
                         xlim = c(-25, 35))
}

title: Sherley Project — Grant Figures
section: 7.3 Adjusted CIF — Excess Dose ≥ +10 % vs Others (Platinum-Related Hospitalisation)
text:
7.3 Adjusted CIF — Excess Dose ≥ +10 % vs Others (Platinum-Related Hospitalisation)
Standardized cumulative incidence contrasting patients whose administered dose was ≥ 10 % above the eGFRCR-CYS-predicted dose (red, “excess”) against all other patients (blue). Same Fine-Gray model, adjusters (age, sex, ecog_score, ici, cockcroft) and g-computation as §6; death is the competing event.


Code
adj_cif_binary("cmp_time_side_effect", "cmp_status_side_effect",
               NULL, "Platinum-Related Hospitalisation — excess dose ≥ +10 % vs others",
               expo_var = "dose_pct_ge10",
               lab_exp  = "Dose discrepancy ≥ +10 % (excess)",
               lab_ref  = "Dose discrepancy < +10 % (others)",
               sub_exp  = "Excess dose ≥ +10%")
